plan.contextChunk: This figure places three small sketched graphs side by side, labeled (a), (b), and (c), each showing curves that rise from left to right on an unmarked vertical axis above a horizontal axis whose tip is labeled n; no numeric ticks appear anywhere. Panel (a) carries three curves: the highest is labeled c2 g(n), the lowest c1 g(n), and a third labeled f(n) weaves between them, dipping and crossing near the left edge before settling into the corridor between the other two. A dashed vertical segment drops from that crossing region to a tick on the n axis marked n0, and the expression f(n) = Theta(g(n)) is printed below the plot. Panel (b) has two curves, the upper labeled c g(n) and the lower labeled f(n); f(n) oscillates sharply at small n, meets c g(n) at the dashed line standing over the tick n0, and runs beneath it from there on, with f(n) = O(g(n)) underneath. Panel (c) reverses the roles, putting f(n) above and c g(n) below after they touch at the dashed n0 line, and is captioned f(n) = Omega(g(n)). Read against one another, the three panels turn on where the labeled curve sits relative to the scaled comparison function once n passes n0, giving the geometric intuition behind bounding a function from both sides, from above only, and from below only.

interactionPlan.concept: Asymptotic notation compares f(n) to a constant-scaled g(n) only for n beyond some threshold n₀: Θ sandwiches f between c₁g and c₂g, O caps it from above, and Ω floors it from below.
elements: Three side-by-side panels sharing a common style, captioned (a), (b), (c)
Each panel: vertical axis with no ticks or numbers, horizontal axis with arrow tip labeled 'n'
Panel (a): upper curve labeled 'c₂g(n)', lower curve labeled 'c₁g(n)', middle wavy curve labeled 'f(n)' that dips and crosses near the left edge before settling between the two
Panel (a) shaded corridor between c₁g(n) and c₂g(n) to the right of n₀ (the permitted region)
Panel (b): upper curve labeled 'cg(n)', lower wavy curve labeled 'f(n)' that oscillates sharply at small n, meets cg(n) at n₀, then stays below
Panel (b) shaded region below cg(n) to the right of n₀
Panel (c): upper curve labeled 'f(n)', lower curve labeled 'cg(n)'; curves touch at n₀ and f(n) stays above afterward
Panel (c) shaded region above cg(n) to the right of n₀
Dashed vertical segment in each panel dropping from the curve-crossing region to the n axis
Tick mark labeled 'n₀' at the foot of each dashed line
Captions under each panel: 'f(n) = Θ(g(n))', 'f(n) = O(g(n))', 'f(n) = Ω(g(n))'
Panel letters (a), (b), (c) below the captions
Violation markers: small red dots/segments on f(n) wherever it leaves the permitted region to the right of n₀
Legend mapping curve colors: f(n) black, scaled g(n) curves blue, permitted region light green tint, violations red

interactions.label: Bound type
interactions.teaches: That the same f(n) and g(n) can satisfy an upper bound, a lower bound, or both, and that Θ is exactly the conjunction of O and Ω.

interactions.label: Threshold n₀
interactions.teaches: That asymptotic bounds are allowed to fail for small n — pushing n₀ right erases early violations, and pulling it left exposes the wild behavior near the origin that the definition deliberately ignores.

interactions.label: Upper constant (c or c₂)
interactions.teaches: That a constant factor can lift the ceiling until f(n) fits underneath — the bound is about growth rate, not about the size of the multiplier.

interactions.label: Lower constant (c or c₁)
interactions.teaches: That shrinking the constant drops the floor until f(n) clears it, showing the lower bound is equally a statement about growth rate.

demo_steps.title: The whole picture
demo_steps.narration: Three panels, one function f(n) compared against scaled copies of the same g(n). In every panel the dashed line at n₀ marks where the promise begins; everything to its left is ignored.

demo_steps.title: Upper bound: f(n) = O(g(n))
demo_steps.narration: Focus on the O panel. The green region is everything at or below cg(n). Past n₀, f(n) never leaves it — that is the entire content of big-O.

demo_steps.title: Shrink c until the bound breaks
demo_steps.narration: Drag the upper constant down. The ceiling drops through f(n) and red violation marks appear to the right of n₀ — the bound now fails, but only because c is too small, not because g grows too slowly.

demo_steps.title: n₀ forgives the early chaos
demo_steps.narration: Restore c and slide n₀ back toward the origin. f(n)'s early oscillations now stick out above the ceiling; sliding n₀ right makes them legal again — 'eventually' is doing real work in the definition.

demo_steps.title: Lower bound: f(n) = Ω(g(n))
demo_steps.narration: Now the floor. With a small enough constant, cg(n) sits under f(n) for all n ≥ n₀ — f grows at least as fast as g.

demo_steps.title: Θ is both at once
demo_steps.narration: Switch to Θ. Now both constants matter: f(n) must stay inside the corridor between c₁g(n) and c₂g(n) past n₀. Squeeze either constant and the corridor closes until violations appear.

demo_steps.title: Close the corridor
demo_steps.narration: Push c₂ down and c₁ up. The green band narrows and f(n) pokes out on both sides — yet a wider pair of constants always exists, which is why f is still Θ(g).

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Asymptotic notation is a claim about a shaded region, not about individual values: pick any constants you like and ignore any finite prefix of inputs — if f(n) can be trapped in that region forever after, the bound holds.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Three equal-width panels in a row on white, hand-drawn textbook style with thin black axes, no tick numbers, each horizontal axis ending in a small arrow labeled italic 'n'. Curves are smooth and monotone-ish increasing overall. In every panel f(n) is drawn in black and starts with a pronounced wiggle (a dip then a hump) in the leftmost fifth before straightening into a gentle rise; the scaled g(n) curves are smooth blue S-shaped rises. Panel (a): two blue curves, the upper labeled c₂g(n) near its right end, the lower labeled c₁g(n), with black f(n) weaving between and labeled between them; tint the corridor between the blue curves light green only to the right of the dashed line. Panel (b): blue cg(n) rises above black f(n) after they meet, labels at the right ends; tint everything below cg(n) light green to the right of n₀. Panel (c): black f(n) on top, blue cg(n) below, labels at right ends; tint above cg(n) to the right of n₀. Each panel has a thin dashed vertical from the curve meeting point down to a small tick on the n axis labeled italic n₀. Italic captions centered under each plot: f(n) = Θ(g(n)), f(n) = O(g(n)), f(n) = Ω(g(n)), with (a), (b), (c) below them. Any portion of f(n) lying outside the green region and right of n₀ should be overdrawn in red with small red dots at the violating samples. Dim non-active panels to ~35% opacity when the toggle selects a single bound type.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for n0: the dashed threshold moves across each plot and violations to its right are marked, making clear that asymptotic bounds only have to hold after a sufficiently large input size.
- Slider for the constant multiplier on g(n): the c g(n), c1 g(n), or c2 g(n) curves move up and down, making clear how constant factors create the allowed upper, lower, or two-sided bound.
- Toggle between Theta, O, and Omega views: the active panel highlights the permitted region for f(n), making clear the difference between two-sided, upper-only, and lower-only comparison.

authoredContext:
Figure 3.1(a) gives an intuitive picture of functions f .n/ and g.n/, where f .n/ D ‚.g.n//. For all values of n at and to the right of n0, the value of f .n/ lies at or above c1g.n/ and at or below c2g.n/. In other words, for all n _x0015_ n0, the function f .n/ is equal to g.n/ to within a constant factor. We say that g.n/ is an asymptotically tight bound for f .n/.
The ‚-notation asymptotically bounds a function from above and below. When
we have only an asymptotic upper bound, we use O-notation. For a given function g.n/, we denote by O.g.n// (pronounced “big-oh of g of n” or sometimes
just “oh of g of n”) the set of functions
O.g.n// D ff .n/ W there exist positive constants c and n0 such that
0 _x0014_ f .n/ _x0014_ cg.n/ for all n _x0015_ n0g :
We use O-notation to give an upper bound on a function, to within a constant
factor. Figure 3.1(b) shows the intuition behind O-notation. For all values n at and
to the right of n0, the value of the function f .n/ is on or below cg.n/.
Just as O-notation provides an asymptotic upper bound on a function, -notation
provides an asymptotic lower bound. For a given function g.n/, we denote
by .g.n// (pronounced “big-omega of g of n” or sometimes just “omega of g
of n”) the set of functions
.g.n// D ff .n/ W there exist positive constants c and n0 such that
0 _x0014_ cg.n/ _x0014_ f .n/ for all n _x0015_ n0g :
Figure 3.1(c) shows the intuition behind -notation. For all values n at or to the
right of n0, the value of f .n/ is on or above cg.n/.
From the definitions of the asymptotic notations we have seen thus far, it is easy
to prove the following important theorem (see Exercise 3.1-5).

discrepancies: The panel letters (a), (b), (c) are clipped at the bottom edge of the figure area — only the tops of the glyphs are visible in the default render.
Scaled-g curves are drawn in blue while the source figure is entirely black line art, so the two-colour scheme changes the overall look.

Large green 'permitted region' fills (unbounded upward in the Ω panel, downward in the O panel) dominate each panel; nothing comparable exists in the source, and in panel (c) the shading covers most of the plot.

Curve morphology differs: the source curves are gentle sigmoids that flatten toward the right, while the generated f(n)/g(n) rise near-vertically at the right edge and f(n) has a tall isolated spike near the origin instead of the source's broad oscillation.

In the source the dashed n₀ line sits exactly at the crossing of f and cg in each panel; here the default n₀ = 30 is placed where the curves are already well separated in panels (a) and (c), weakening the 'bound starts to hold here' reading.
A colour legend strip (f(n), scaled g(n), permitted region, violation) is added under the controls; no legend exists in the source.
evaluation.notes: Three-panel Θ/O/Ω composition with correct labels, captions and dashed n₀ lines is well reproduced and the slider/step interactions are genuinely pedagogical, but the added blue colouring and heavy green corridors shift the visual identity away from the all-black source and the (a)/(b)/(c) panel letters are clipped at the bottom.
action_items: Increase bottom layout padding (or reduce caption offsets) so the (a), (b), (c) letters render fully inside the canvas instead of being cut off.
Draw the scaled-g curves in black (matching the source) by default and reserve colour for the interactive highlight/violation state, or at least soften the blue toward near-black.
Reduce the opacity/extent of the green permitted-region fill — clip it to a band near the curves rather than filling the whole half-plane, especially in the Ω panel.
Reshape f(n) and g(n) to the source's flatter sigmoid profile (plateau then gentle rise) and default n₀ to the f/cg crossing point in each panel so the static state matches the textbook figure.

feedback.rationale: The three-panel concept, interactions and labels are correct; the issues are implementation-level (clipped panel letters, color scheme, over-extended fills, curve shaping and default n₀), so the generator should refine the rendering.

plan.concept: Asymptotic notation compares f(n) to a constant-scaled g(n) only for n beyond some threshold n₀: Θ sandwiches f between c₁g and c₂g, O caps it from above, and Ω floors it from below.
elements: Three side-by-side panels sharing a common style, captioned (a), (b), (c)
Each panel: vertical axis with no ticks or numbers, horizontal axis with arrow tip labeled 'n'
Panel (a): upper curve labeled 'c₂g(n)', lower curve labeled 'c₁g(n)', middle wavy curve labeled 'f(n)' that dips and crosses near the left edge before settling between the two
Panel (a) shaded corridor between c₁g(n) and c₂g(n) to the right of n₀ (the permitted region)
Panel (b): upper curve labeled 'cg(n)', lower wavy curve labeled 'f(n)' that oscillates sharply at small n, meets cg(n) at n₀, then stays below
Panel (b) shaded region below cg(n) to the right of n₀
Panel (c): upper curve labeled 'f(n)', lower curve labeled 'cg(n)'; curves touch at n₀ and f(n) stays above afterward
Panel (c) shaded region above cg(n) to the right of n₀
Dashed vertical segment in each panel dropping from the curve-crossing region to the n axis
Tick mark labeled 'n₀' at the foot of each dashed line
Captions under each panel: 'f(n) = Θ(g(n))', 'f(n) = O(g(n))', 'f(n) = Ω(g(n))'
Panel letters (a), (b), (c) below the captions
Violation markers: small red dots/segments on f(n) wherever it leaves the permitted region to the right of n₀
Legend mapping curve colors: f(n) black, scaled g(n) curves blue, permitted region light green tint, violations red

interactions.label: Bound type
interactions.teaches: That the same f(n) and g(n) can satisfy an upper bound, a lower bound, or both, and that Θ is exactly the conjunction of O and Ω.

interactions.label: Threshold n₀
interactions.teaches: That asymptotic bounds are allowed to fail for small n — pushing n₀ right erases early violations, and pulling it left exposes the wild behavior near the origin that the definition deliberately ignores.

interactions.label: Upper constant (c or c₂)
interactions.teaches: That a constant factor can lift the ceiling until f(n) fits underneath — the bound is about growth rate, not about the size of the multiplier.

interactions.label: Lower constant (c or c₁)
interactions.teaches: That shrinking the constant drops the floor until f(n) clears it, showing the lower bound is equally a statement about growth rate.

demo_steps.title: The whole picture
demo_steps.narration: Three panels, one function f(n) compared against scaled copies of the same g(n). In every panel the dashed line at n₀ marks where the promise begins; everything to its left is ignored.

demo_steps.title: Upper bound: f(n) = O(g(n))
demo_steps.narration: Focus on the O panel. The green region is everything at or below cg(n). Past n₀, f(n) never leaves it — that is the entire content of big-O.

demo_steps.title: Shrink c until the bound breaks
demo_steps.narration: Drag the upper constant down. The ceiling drops through f(n) and red violation marks appear to the right of n₀ — the bound now fails, but only because c is too small, not because g grows too slowly.

demo_steps.title: n₀ forgives the early chaos
demo_steps.narration: Restore c and slide n₀ back toward the origin. f(n)'s early oscillations now stick out above the ceiling; sliding n₀ right makes them legal again — 'eventually' is doing real work in the definition.

demo_steps.title: Lower bound: f(n) = Ω(g(n))
demo_steps.narration: Now the floor. With a small enough constant, cg(n) sits under f(n) for all n ≥ n₀ — f grows at least as fast as g.

demo_steps.title: Θ is both at once
demo_steps.narration: Switch to Θ. Now both constants matter: f(n) must stay inside the corridor between c₁g(n) and c₂g(n) past n₀. Squeeze either constant and the corridor closes until violations appear.

demo_steps.title: Close the corridor
demo_steps.narration: Push c₂ down and c₁ up. The green band narrows and f(n) pokes out on both sides — yet a wider pair of constants always exists, which is why f is still Θ(g).

plan.keyInsight: Asymptotic notation is a claim about a shaded region, not about individual values: pick any constants you like and ignore any finite prefix of inputs — if f(n) can be trapped in that region forever after, the bound holds.
plan.reconstructionNotes: Three equal-width panels in a row on white, hand-drawn textbook style with thin black axes, no tick numbers, each horizontal axis ending in a small arrow labeled italic 'n'. Curves are smooth and monotone-ish increasing overall. In every panel f(n) is drawn in black and starts with a pronounced wiggle (a dip then a hump) in the leftmost fifth before straightening into a gentle rise; the scaled g(n) curves are smooth blue S-shaped rises. Panel (a): two blue curves, the upper labeled c₂g(n) near its right end, the lower labeled c₁g(n), with black f(n) weaving between and labeled between them; tint the corridor between the blue curves light green only to the right of the dashed line. Panel (b): blue cg(n) rises above black f(n) after they meet, labels at the right ends; tint everything below cg(n) light green to the right of n₀. Panel (c): black f(n) on top, blue cg(n) below, labels at right ends; tint above cg(n) to the right of n₀. Each panel has a thin dashed vertical from the curve meeting point down to a small tick on the n axis labeled italic n₀. Italic captions centered under each plot: f(n) = Θ(g(n)), f(n) = O(g(n)), f(n) = Ω(g(n)), with (a), (b), (c) below them. Any portion of f(n) lying outside the green region and right of n₀ should be overdrawn in red with small red dots at the violating samples. Dim non-active panels to ~35% opacity when the toggle selects a single bound type.

discrepancies: In the source, f(n) crosses the scaled g(n) curves exactly at the dashed n₀ line in all three panels (that crossing is what defines n₀). In the generated default state (n₀=25, c=2/0.7) f(n) lies comfortably between the bounds with no crossing at n₀, so the dashed line looks arbitrary rather than marking the point where the bound begins to hold.

The characteristic early oscillation of f(n) (a sharp dip then a tall hump that pokes above/below g in panels b and c) is much flatter and smaller in the generated curves, so the 'chaotic prefix forgiven by n₀' visual story is weakened.

Panel sizing: each panel renders only ~190×200 px inside a much taller container, leaving large empty bands above and below the row; the whole figure reads much smaller than the source and pushes all text near the minimum legible size.

In the source, the y-axis left edge shows the curves entering at distinct heights with c₁g(n) nearly horizontal at the far left; the generated curves are compressed near the origin and the leftmost plateau of the lower bound is not visible as in the original.

Generated adds a legend block (green permitted region, red violation, blue g colouring) and tinted/red overlays not in the source — acceptable as UI chrome, but the colour-coded legend is visible even at step 0 where none of those elements are drawn.
evaluation.notes: Three-panel Θ/O/Ω composition with correct curve labels, dashed n₀, arrowed n-axis and captions is faithfully reproduced and backed by a genuinely rich interaction set (step player, bound selector, n₀ and two constant sliders, tooltips, popups), but the panels render too small with wasted vertical space, making all text borderline legible, and the default state omits the curve/bound crossings at n₀ that give the original figure its meaning.

Tune the default n₀ / c values (or f and g) so that at step 0 f(n) actually intersects c₁g, c₂g and cg at the dashed n₀ line in each panel, exactly as in the textbook figure.
Amplify the early dip-and-hump of f(n) so that it visibly violates the bound to the left of n₀ in panels (b) and (c), matching the source silhouette.
Hide or grey out the colour legend entries (green permitted region, red violation, blue g) until those overlays are actually active, so the step-0 state is a clean drop-in for the static figure.
